title: Checkpoint-Store Threat Model
summary: Framework-independent threat model treating the orchestration checkpoint blob as a deserialization trust boundary, listing implemented controls and unbuilt ones.
scope: run id generation and cross-run contamination
notes: Manifest declared DOC/precedence 9; heuristic (path docs/handoff/) and content analysis agree. Content carries a status line ('complete — an ADR-012 spike deliverable') and a threat/mitigation table, which are SPEC-adjacent signals, but section 7 states explicitly 'It does not select a candidate' — this is evidence and security analysis supporting ADR-012, not the decision and not an implementation contract. Classified DOC per manifest; treat as context plus a source of outstanding requirements. IMPORTANT for the synthesizer: section 5 lists controls ALREADY BUILT (store JSON not objects and re-validate through Pydantic contracts on load; JsonPlusSerializer(pickle_fallback=False, allowed_msgpack_modules=None) constructed in code rather than via LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK env var; never pickle, asserted by test; exact pins plus pip-audit in CI). Section 6 lists controls NOT built — capture each as an OUTSTANDING REQUIREMENT / Milestone 2 forward work, never as a completed control: (1) ROW-LEVEL INTEGRITY — a keyed MAC over serialized checkpoint state, computed with a key the database role cannot read, verified on load; described as the single largest gap and the control that converts threats T2 (findings altered before review) and T3 (review gate skipped) from difficult to detectable; NOT BUILT. (2) LEAST-PRIVILEGE DATABASE ROLES — spike runs as a single superuser-ish role; production needs a checkpoint-write role separate from everything else and from the migration role; NOT BUILT. (3) ENCRYPTION AT REST AND BACKUP HANDLING — assumed platform-provided in GovCloud, explicitly tagged [unverified], rides on Q-01. (4) CHECKPOINT RETENTION AND PRUNING — no policy exists for how long a checkpoint carrying case-derived text is kept; ties to Q-09; material given measured history growth of 37,033 bytes of thread storage against a 16,115-byte latest checkpoint for three findings. (5) PROVENANCE ON LOAD — a resumed run does not record which checkpoint id it resumed from into the run manifest, so an audit cannot reconstruct the resume chain; noted as cheap to add. Two other design constraints worth carrying forward: strict deserialization fails SOFT (a refused value returns as a plain dict, not an exception), which is why contract re-validation on load is load-bearing rather than defense-in-depth; and run ids must be server-generated, never client-supplied, with attention to PostgresSaver truncating thread_id at a length-limited column, since a truncating id scheme could create cross-run collisions.
